A.reason: All candidates respect the hard constraints and check availability, condition, cleanup and seated access. Distinct mechanisms are centralized return processing, reader reshelving through visible destinations, an on-site reserve, optional shared tidying, and portable return reminders. Candidate 1 best supports immediate availability and routine self-maintenance with modest volunteer effort; its pilot checks whether sorting and missed damage offset those benefits.

B.reason: All candidates are usable without definite serious hard-constraint violations. Candidates 0 and 5 share centralized return processing; 5 adds a capacity repair rather than a new primary mechanism. Other mechanisms are visible reshelving destinations, an on-site reserve, shared tidying, reader condition screening, and departure-stage borrowing decisions. Candidate 5 offers the strongest operational plan: it checks capacity, preserves access and availability during overflow, and specifies when to abandon mandatory box returns within the volunteer budget.

pair.reason: B5 narrowly beats A1 through explicit handling of full boxes, interrupted processing and repeated workload overruns, with inspectable fallback triggers. A1 offers a strong self-maintaining ritual, but its response to sorting or inspection workload exceeding the available visits is less concrete. Neither proposal establishes effectiveness before the pilot.
